title: Underfitting
subtitle: Topic: Underfitting · Subject: Supervised Machine Learning. Three beginner, two medium and two advanced questions; seven custom SVG instructional diagrams; realistic choices and concise beginner-first explanations.
hero:
UNDERFITTING · VISUAL STUDY

When the model cannot learn an important pattern

Underfitting often appears when a model or its features are too limited to capture useful structure. Learn the training-versus-validation clues, high-bias patterns, practical remedies and the risks of making a model too complex.

questions.stem: What is Underfitting in supervised machine learning, and why might a straight-line model fail when the target follows a strong nonlinear relationship?
options: Underfitting means a model has memorized individual training examples so closely that it performs poorly only on new observations. A straight line is most likely to underfit because it has too many adjustable parameters.

Underfitting occurs whenever test error is larger than training error, even if the model fits training observations very well. A straight-line model underfits only when its predictions fluctuate too sharply across nearby inputs.

Underfitting occurs when a model fails to capture important structure even in its training examples, often because its capacity or features are insufficient. A straight line can miss a curved target relationship.

Underfitting means a trained model gives different predictions each time it receives exactly the same input. A straight line cannot avoid underfitting because prediction consistency requires using a nonlinear activation for every output.
questions.explanation: Explanation: Underfitting means the model cannot adequately represent or learn the important patterns in the training data. A straight-line regression model cannot follow a strongly curved relationship, so its errors remain substantial even on examples it was trained to fit. This is often called a high-bias problem. Imagine trying to predict electricity demand as temperatures become very cold or very hot. A simple line may overlook that demand rises at both extremes. Underfitting is about inadequate fit, not merely any disappointing test score.
questions.figure:
QUESTION 01 · UNDERFITTING

The true examples follow a nonlinear pattern but a straight-line model misses that structure on the training set. Underfitting indicates insufficient fit, not just a disappointing test score.

questions.stem: What pattern in training and validation errors suggests Underfitting, and how does it differ from the typical error pattern of overfitting?
options: Underfitting often produces high training error and similarly high validation error, because the model cannot explain even seen examples. Overfitting more typically shows low training error but much higher validation error.

Underfitting typically produces almost zero training error and very high validation error, because the model has memorized training labels. Overfitting instead produces high error on both datasets with almost no difference.

Underfitting is defined by validation error being slightly greater than training error, regardless of their absolute values. Overfitting occurs whenever validation error is lower than training error, even for strong models.

Underfitting produces high validation accuracy with low training accuracy because the model learns better from unseen cases. Overfitting produces low error on both datasets whenever training includes enough examples.
questions.explanation: Explanation: When a model underfits, it struggles on training examples and usually also performs poorly on validation examples. For instance, training loss 8 and validation loss 9 suggest that the model has not learned enough to fit either set. An overfit model might have training loss 1 but validation loss 9, revealing a large generalization gap. These numbers are illustrative and must be judged against the task's baseline and metric. A high validation loss alone does not tell you which problem you have.
questions.figure:
QUESTION 02 · UNDERFITTING

In this illustrative comparison, underfit training and validation errors are 8 and 9. An overfit model has low training error 1 but high validation error 9.

questions.stem: Which conditions can cause Underfitting, and why is it important to distinguish insufficient model capacity from incomplete optimization or missing data features?
options: Underfitting occurs only because a training dataset contains too few examples, so collecting more samples is always the first fix. Missing features and overly strong regularization cannot cause a low training score.

Underfitting requires unusually large models that learn noise, so removing regularization and increasing depth always make the problem worse. Optimization progress is irrelevant once a model has seen one training batch.

Underfitting is caused by evaluation metrics giving different values for training and validation data, not by model design. Using the same metric on both sets guarantees that the model can learn the target pattern.

Insufficient capacity, weak features and excessive regularization can limit the model's fit. Stopping optimization before convergence can look similar, so checking learning progress helps choose an appropriate remedy rather than blindly adding complexity.
questions.explanation: Explanation: A model may fit poorly because its representation is too restrictive, important predictive inputs are missing, or regularization suppresses useful flexibility. A different problem can look similar if the optimizer has not trained long enough or has unsuitable settings. For example, a shallow decision tree may be unable to separate customer behavior patterns, while a capable neural network might simply need better training. Check both the model's capacity and its optimization progress before changing its size. More complexity is not a universal solution.
questions.figure:
QUESTION 03 · UNDERFITTING

Underfitting can reflect insufficient representational capacity, missing informative features or overly strong regularization. A model stopped before convergence may look similar but needs an optimization diagnosis.

questions.stem: How can learning curves help diagnose Underfitting, and what do persistently high, closely spaced training and validation errors imply as the number of examples increases?
options: High and closely spaced learning curves indicate that adding more data will necessarily solve the model's problem, since data volume always increases the expressiveness of a fixed linear or shallow hypothesis class.

Training and validation errors that remain high and close as more examples arrive can indicate high bias. Adding data alone may help little without improving features, capacity or training, so compare the curves with a baseline.

High training and validation errors prove the model has learned every training example exactly, with the remaining discrepancy caused by evaluation noise. The only appropriate intervention is stronger regularization.

Learning curves diagnose underfitting only when training loss decreases to zero while validation loss keeps rising. When both errors stay high, the curves imply perfect generalization even if the predictions are consistently inaccurate.
questions.explanation: Explanation: A learning curve shows how performance changes as the training sample count increases. If training error and validation error approach a similarly high plateau, the model may be limited by bias or insufficiently useful features. Merely adding more observations might not teach a straight line to represent a curved relationship. For example, adding thousands of more temperature records does not give a linear model a quadratic feature automatically. Compare performance with a naive baseline and investigate label quality or training convergence before assuming capacity is the sole cause.
questions.figure:
QUESTION 04 · UNDERFITTING

When training and validation errors remain high and close as more examples are added, the model may be high-bias. More data alone may have limited benefit without changing representation or fitting.

questions.stem: What does a scikit-learn comparison of polynomial degrees 1 and 3 reveal about Underfitting when data are generated from a nonlinear relationship?
options: Degree 1 is better because fewer features always lower both training and test error. Degree 3 must overfit immediately, since representing a cubic relationship requires memorizing each training observation separately.

Degree 1 and degree 3 must have identical training loss because polynomial features do not change what LinearRegression can express. Differences in measured test error arise entirely from the random train/test split.

On the tested nonlinear dataset, degree 1 has training/test MSE 13.52/16.79, while degree 3 improves them to 4.68/5.79. Capturing the cubic structure reduces underfitting, though greater complexity is not always better.
Degree 3 is better because the holdout examples are included when fitting its polynomial transform. Training on the full dataset before splitting is what makes the nonlinear model generalize well.
questions.explanation: Explanation: PolynomialFeatures expands a model's available input terms. A degree-1 model can represent a straight line but cannot capture the cubic structure deliberately built into this synthetic dataset. A degree-3 model can represent that pattern, improving both training and held-out mean squared error. The reproducible code reports degree 1: 13.52 train and 16.79 test; degree 3: 4.68 train and 5.79 test. This is evidence of underfitting by the simpler model in this example, not proof that every higher-degree model will generalize.
questions.figure:
QUESTION 05 · UNDERFITTING
scikit-learn · Degree 1 versus Degree 3 15 lines
import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import PolynomialFeatures
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error
rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
X = np.linspace(-3, 3, 100).reshape(-1, 1)
y = .8*X[:,0]**3 - 2*X[:,0] + rng.normal(0, 2.5, 100)
Xtr, Xte, ytr, yte = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=.25, random_state=42)
for d in [1, 3]:
    model = make_pipeline(PolynomialFeatures(d, include_bias=False), LinearRegression())
    model.fit(Xtr, ytr)
    train = mean_squared_error(ytr, model.predict(Xtr))
    print(d, round(train, 2), round(mean_squared_error(yte, model.predict(Xte)), 2))

On 100 synthetic nonlinear samples split 75/25, degree-1 regression has train/test MSE 13.52/16.79; degree-3 regression improves them to 4.68/5.79.

questions.stem: Which targeted interventions can reduce Underfitting, and why should every increase in flexibility or change in regularization be checked against validation performance?
options: Useful interventions may include more informative features, a model able to represent nonlinear patterns, relaxing excessive regularization, or completing optimization. Recheck both training and validation errors because extra flexibility can eventually overfit.

An underfitting model should always receive stronger regularization and fewer input features, since shrinking its coefficients guarantees lower training loss. Validation results are unnecessary once the model becomes simpler.

Collecting more training samples always eliminates underfitting, even if the model cannot express the true relationship. Choosing the most complex architecture is therefore unnecessary and can be replaced entirely by dataset size.

To fix underfitting, repeatedly tune model architecture against the final test set until its score is maximized. The resulting estimate remains unbiased because training and testing use different data partitions.
questions.explanation: Explanation: A good remedy addresses why the model fits poorly. Better input features or a more expressive model can represent missed structure; weaker excessive regularization can free useful coefficients; improved optimization can let a capable model finish learning. After each change, inspect both training error and validation performance. For example, increasing tree depth may help a very shallow classifier separate customer groups but can later overfit noise. Tune with validation or cross-validation, not by repeatedly choosing settings on the final test set.
questions.figure:
QUESTION 06 · UNDERFITTING

Try informative features, a more flexible hypothesis class, weaker excessive regularization, or enough optimization steps, depending on the diagnosis. Track training and validation performance after each change.

questions.tag: Advanced · Diagnosis, baselines and evaluation integrity
questions.stem: How should Underfitting be diagnosed when poor scores might instead come from noisy labels, unsuitable optimization, data leakage, or a challenging validation distribution?
options: Poor validation performance always proves the hypothesis class is too small, so train on the combined training and test datasets before diagnosing the model. Data quality and convergence checks are unnecessary for this conclusion.

A large gap between training and validation loss always means underfitting, so reduce regularization until the gap disappears. Final model selection can safely reuse the same test observations many times.

Compare only the final test accuracy with a fixed target, ignoring training performance or baseline models. A model that misses the target must underfit regardless of whether examples are noisy or evaluation is shifted.

Compare a naive baseline, training fit, validation gap and optimization progress; check features and label quality. Use validation data for improvements, preserve a final untouched test set, and investigate group or time shifts.
questions.explanation: Explanation: Poor scores have several causes. Compare a simple baseline first, then see whether the model fits training data and whether validation error is much worse. Check convergence, informative features, label quality and whether training and validation distributions differ. A model may be hard to train or face noisy outcomes rather than simply being too small. Fit preprocessing on training data only, tune using validation or cross-validation, and reserve test data for final evaluation. Use chronological or group-aware splits when related observations could leak.
questions.figure:
QUESTION 07 · UNDERFITTING

Compare with a simple baseline, check convergence and training error, inspect the validation gap, and tune fixes on validation or cross-validation rather than repeatedly examining test data.
